title: What's New in Vesence: July 2026
summary: July went into the web app: real editors for everything an agent touches, a home for every matter, tasks that hold several conversations at once, tools your own firm can build, and a way to work in the systems you already run.
body_markdown:
## The Web App


Almost everything we shipped in July points in one direction: the web app. Vesence began as an intelligence layer inside Microsoft Office, and Word, Outlook, Excel, and PowerPoint are still where the work gets finished. But the place people direct that work from has become the web.


Chat.


One workspace: the chat opens on its own, then hands the window over as you move through email, calendar, SharePoint, and the term sheet.


So July went into The Agentic Workspace: one place to hand over a piece of work, watch it happen, and take it back whenever you want. Five things stand out.


## 1. Write and Edit Without Leaving the Chat


Emails, documents, spreadsheets, presentations, Teams messages. You can now write and edit every one of them in the chat itself. Each opens in a real editor, not a preview, so changing a sentence no longer means downloading a file.


Every change an agent proposes arrives as a tracked change. Step through them one at a time, accept, reject, or type over them yourself. Your formatting holds throughout. More in[Introducing Vesence Editor](https://www.vesence.com/blog/vesence-editor) .


## 2. A Home for Every Matter


Most work isn't a single question. A matter runs for weeks around the same files, the same colleagues, and the same way of doing things. A project holds all of it — files, chats, and drafts — shared with your team.


The files and the instructions sit on the project, so every chat inside it already knows the matter. Nobody starts from scratch, and neither does an agent. It sits alongside SharePoint and your document management system rather than replacing either. More in[Introducing Vesence Projects](https://www.vesence.com/blog/vesence-projects) .


## 3. One Task, Several Conversations


A task can now hold more than one chat. Large work splits into separate conversations that stay together under a single objective: one drafting the agreement, one checking the cross-references, one working through the counterparty's comments.


It's a shape more than a feature. When a dozen things are underway at once, you can still see what's running, what's finished, and what needs you.


## 4. Build the Tools Your Team Needs


Introducing the Vesence App Store. Describe the tool you wish you had, and the agent builds it. A chronology tracker. A cap table reconciler. Something that watches the conditions precedent and tells you what's still outstanding.


Publish it to your firm's library and it appears for everyone, the next time they look. Every firm ends up with its own small set of tools, built by the people who actually do the work. More in[Introducing Vesence Apps](https://www.vesence.com/blog/introducing-vesence-apps) .


## 5. It Works With the Systems You Already Run


Your time recording. Your billing. Your accounting, and the templates your documents are built from. Agents can now work in those systems the same way they work in Word and Excel.


Nothing has to be built for each one. You describe how your system works, and the agent learns to operate it directly — the same way it already opens and edits your Office files. So connecting the next system is a conversation, not a project.


## What This Adds Up To


Put together, July moves Vesence from somewhere you ask questions to somewhere work gets done. Your colleagues, your files, your systems, and the agents working alongside them, in one place. You decide what happens. It happens in the tools you already use.
